newsitem.title: USA: Chubais sees Russian economic growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Chubais sees Russian economic growth in 1998.

text.p: The Russian economy should grow next year after five difficult years of economic reform, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Sunday.

Chubais, who is also Russian Finance Minister, told NBC's Meet the Press program that 22 percent of Russians were now living below the poverty line, but growth would mean that Russian living standards would rise.
"For the first time we are on the real eve of economic growth, which means the growth of standards of living...and I am sure that 1998 will be the first year of Russian economic growth," he said.

Ministers initially predicted growth this year, but they have scaled back this forecast in recent months. Output has halved in the years since Russia launched its economic reform program, designed to turn the communist-era centrally planned economy into a market system like that in the West.
Chubais, in Denver with President Boris Yeltsin to attend the summit of the Group of Seven industrializd countries, said Russia had already become a "viable and capitalist society".
Asked if communism was dead in Russia, he replied: "Absolutely."
